title: Cognitive Augmentation, Remediation, and TDCS for Schizophrenia
official: Cognitive Augmentation, Remediation, and TDCS for Schizophrenia (CARTS)
summary:
Schizophrenia-spectrum disorders (SSDs; schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, etc.) are among the most disabling and costly conditions globally. Most SSD medications treat symptoms like hallucinations and delusions, but cognitive symptoms, or problems with thinking, memory, and problem solving, remain untreated by medication. Other developing treatments for these symptoms include noninvasive stimulation of cognitive brain regions and behavioral therapies involving mental skill-building activities. While both of these treatments appear to improve cognitive symptoms, effects are inconsistent depending on specific details of the trial. Growing evidence suggests that using these therapies together could lead to larger, clinically meaningful effects. Still, prior combined therapy trials use simplified versions of the behavioral therapy, omitting the guidance of a therapist to engage and challenge the participant. These previous trials show some evidence for beneficial effects, particularly in working memory, but the omission of a therapist could limit effects. This study will be the first to test if using a comprehensive, therapist-guided behavioral therapy can amplify the effects of noninvasive brain stimulation (NIBS) to reduce cognitive symptoms and change brain activity in SSDs. We will conduct a small pilot study to gather preliminary evidence for this combined therapy using 10 participants split into 2 groups. One group will receive NIBS and comprehensive cognitive therapy (NIBS+) while the other receives NIBS and performs quizzes without the guidance of a therapist (NIBS-). Participants will receive therapies for 10 days over 2 weeks with 2 hours of therapy per day. We will compare interventions through the following aims. Aim 1 will examine changes in brain connections after NIBS+ and NIBS-. We will collect data from electrical brain recordings (electroencephalography/EEG) before and after interventions. We expect that connections between cognitive brain regions will be most strengthened by NIBS+ compared to NIBS-. Aim 2 will investigate what kind of cognitive symptoms are affected by NIBS+ and NIBS-. We will perform cognitive tests before and after the interventions. We expect that all cognitive symptoms (memory, motor speed, language skills, attention, processing speed, and planning abilities) will be most improved by NIBS+ compared to NIBS-, but that the largest improvements will be in short-term, active memory skills ("working memory"). We will also investigate if there is a relationship between the changes in brain connections and cognitive improvements.

This preliminary study will provide early evidence that the effects of noninvasive brain stimulation can be strengthened by a structured, therapist-guided behavioral therapy for cognitive symptoms. This will support the development of a new, combined therapy for untreated cognitive symptoms in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. We will use findings of this study to support a trial proposal to the National Institute of Mental Health to test this therapy in a larger group of individuals.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of schizophrenia, schizoaffective disorder, or schizophreniform disorder
* Proficient in English
* IQ \>= 80

Exclusion Criteria:

* Major neurological conditions
* Implanted devices in the body or metal in the head
* Changes to relevant medications within 1 month of enrollment
* Pregnancy or breastfeeding
* Moderate to severe DSM V substance use disorder
* Clinical instability including recent or severe suicidal ideation or actions
* Positive urine drug screen for illicit substances
* Skin allergy to lidocaine or electrolyte gel
